what_happened: The operator queued seven records-history steps. Dependencies were written in words ("depends on job 7 part 2"), and acceptance was written inline. `athena plan` reads dependencies only from job ids in the text and reads acceptance only from bullets. It didn't see the worded dependencies, so it put job 8 (remove records/ from main) ahead of the cutover. A drain would have run them in that order. It also didn't parse the inline acceptance, so all seven items were held. The operator caught it before any drain.
cause: The accepted request format is implicit. It is not documented where requests are written, and the intake commands (`athena ask --later`, `athena plan`) accept any free text without checking that the parts the planner depends on can be parsed. Input the parser ignores is dropped silently, and the failure shows up only as a wrong plan order or held items. A misordered plan that is destructive if drained has no check either.
prevention: Add a lint at `athena ask --later` and `athena plan`. It would (1) warn or refuse when the text names a dependency in words ("depends on", "after job N", "part 2") with no parsable job id, (2) warn when no acceptance bullets are found, and (3) print the parsed dependencies and acceptance next to the plan so a mismatch is visible before a drain. Also document the format (acceptance as bullets, dependencies as job ids) in the request-writing guide.
proposed_request: Make `athena ask --later` and `athena plan` check the request format before queuing. Outcomes: (1) If a request names a dependency in words (for example "depends on job 7 part 2", "after the cutover") without a parsable job id, the command warns and says which phrase was not parsed, or refuses unless the operator passes an explicit override. (2) If a request has no acceptance bullets, the command warns that inline acceptance is not parsed and says the item will be held. (3) `athena plan` prints, for each item, the dependencies and acceptance it parsed, so the operator can compare them with what they meant. (4) The request format (acceptance as bullets, dependencies as job ids) is documented in the place where requests are written. Acceptance: tests show that a worded dependency produces a warning and a request with inline-only acceptance produces a warning. A request with job-id dependencies and bullet acceptance produces neither, and the plan output lists the parsed dependencies and acceptance.
